transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-19 15:00 PST | Duration: 52 mins | Recording ID: ff-20261119-silkroad-001

Attendees:
- Maya Chen (Redwood AE)
- Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE)
- Rae Patel (Redwood Partnerships)
- Priya Kapoor (SilkRoad, CTO)
- Liam O'Connor (SilkRoad, Head of Platform)
- Anita Sengupta (SilkRoad, Infra Lead)
- Jonas Berg (SilkRoad, Solutions Architect)

00:00 Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick intros, then we can jump into what you're trying to solve.
00:13 Priya: Hi, Priya here, CTO at SilkRoad. We're exploring ways to offer GPU-backed LLM inference to our SaaS customers without building a full infra stack. We're interested in two things: a reseller onramp and managed onramp models.
00:28 Liam: Yeah and from platform side we care about tenancy, SLAs, and how billing flows if we resell.
00:39 Maya: Great, that's exactly what Redwood helps partners with. Diego, want to frame the technical options?
00:44 Diego: Sure. Broadly there are three patterns: 1) resell hosted API where SilkRoad bills customers and we provide partner pricing and routing, 2) managed onramp where SilkRoad runs a thin control plane and we host inference either in dedicated pools, or 3) private deployment — VPC/on-prem variants. Each has tradeoffs on latency, data residency, and integration complexity.
01:05 Anita: When you say "dedicated pools" do you mean a persistent GPU cluster we can route to, or ephemeral burst capacity? Our customers are latency sensitive.
01:15 Diego: Good question. We support reserved dedicated capacity with guaranteed throughput and latency SLOs — that's Redwood Dedicated — and also burstable capacity for spiky workloads. For reseller you'd typically map tenants to a dedicated pool to preserve latencies.
01:29 Jonas (murmur): Hmm okay.
01:33 Priya: Security is big for us. We need to know about KMS integrations, audit logs for model inputs/outputs, and SSO/SAML for multi-tenant visibility.
01:44 Rae: On the partnerships side, we can support co-branded routes and offer partner-level dashboards. On security, Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and full audit trail. Diego can give the specifics.
01:57 Diego: For KMS we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations — you control the keys, we never persist them in plaintext. Audit logs are shipped to your logging endpoint and we have token-level tracing in Console. Note: redaction options exist if you want to avoid storing full PII in the logs.
02:17 Liam: Is the audit log retention configurable per partner? Some of our customers need 7 years, others 90 days.
02:24 Diego: Console supports configurable retention windows but for multi-year retention you'd typically route logs to your own archival S3/long-term store — we can forward.
02:31 Priya: Network question — can Redwood peer into our VPC, or do we have to NAT outbound to Redwood endpoints? Our customers prefer private peering.
02:43 Diego: We support VPC peering and private connectivity. Two common flows: 1) you peer and we route traffic on private network, or 2) we ship an on-prem/private package for air-gapped customers. Peering requires some firewall and routing config which we'd document.
02:58 Anita: Any constraints on MTU or TCP keepalives? We run some latency-sensitive streams.
03:05 Diego: There are recommendations — we'll provide an integration checklist. Usually MTU isn't an issue but keepalives and idle timeouts can affect long-lived streams. We'll share the exact network playbook.
03:17 Priya: What about model variants and quantization? Some of our customers only want deterministic outputs and can't tolerate hallucinations.
03:27 Diego: We provide model cataloging and can pin model versions per route. Quantized variants are supported for cost/latency tradeoffs but deterministic behavior depends on sampling parameters; we can offer conservative settings plus evals to validate. Part of the pilot is picking model variants and running eval prompts.
03:44 Maya: Curious — what's your expected QPS and concurrency for an MVP pilot?
03:49 Liam: For the initial cohort maybe 50 QPS steady with spikes to 400 during peak windows.
03:56 Diego: That's useful. For 50–400 QPS we'll likely recommend a small dedicated pool with autoscale headroom and prefix caching. Caching will reduce token cost for repeated prompts.
04:10 Priya: On the commercial side, how do you structure partner pricing? Revenue share? Wholesale rates?
04:16 Rae: We typically do tiered partner pricing + an uplift for white-label or reseller bundles. There are options: revenue share split, fixed committed capacity with a discount, or pass-through with partner margin. We can walk through sample models in the playbook.
04:31 Priya: And billing is monthly? We need invoices we can programmatically ingest.
04:35 Rae: Yes, monthly billing with CSV and API exports for usage. We also support per-route tagging so you can reconcile per-customer usage.
04:44 Jonas: Any partner requirements around SOC 2 / ISO? A lot of our customers ask for that.
04:50 Maya: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II and pursuing ISO. We can share the compliance pack after an NDA.
04:58 Anita: On ops — how do you handle upgrades/rollouts? We don't want model regressions hitting customers.
05:05 Diego: We have rollout policies — canary deploys, A/B tests, automatic fallback to previous variant on regression. We also tie regressions to prompt sets so you can catch quality drops before they hit production.
05:19 Priya: For a pilot, we'd want a canary with 5% traffic, run a smoke set, then expand.
05:25 Diego: Totally doable, and we'll instrument the evaluation hooks.
05:28 Maya: A couple quick operational specifics — SLA targets for Dedicated: 99.9% availability and 99th percentile latency targets per model. For reseller flows we can carve SLAs into the partner contract.
05:42 Liam: Great. One corner case — we have customers in EU that require data residency and GDPR controls. Can we route those requests to EU-only instances?
05:51 Diego: Yes, routing by region is supported and you can pin region-specific model endpoints. We also support data residency controls in Private deployments.
05:59 Priya: Any tricky bits if we want to embed inference into our existing multi-tenant orchestration? We handle tenants via our own routing layer.
06:09 Diego: As long as you pass tenant identifiers and apply per-tenant routing rules, Redwood's routing policies will map requests to dedicated pools or variants. We'll provide SDK snippets for common languages.
06:20 Jonas: Will you provide a partner API to programmatically spin workloads up or is that manual?
06:26 Rae: Partners get a partner API and a console portal. There are programmatic endpoints for capacity reservations, model pinning, and usage exports.
06:36 Priya: Perf testing — can we run our benchmarks against a dedicated pool before committing?
06:42 Diego: Absolutely. We recommend a short perf run (48–72 hours) with traffic profile and KV/prefix caching enabled to capture realistic perf. We'll provide a benchmark harness and a checklist.
06:55 Liam: About support — will we have a dedicated technical account manager during pilot?
06:59 Maya: Yes, pilots come with a Solutions Engineer and priority support. Post-pilot we can scope a TAM as needed.
07:07 Priya: Ok so next steps?
07:09 Maya: Action items: we'll send the partner playbook, sample commercial terms, and the network/security integration checklist. SilkRoad to share network diagram and target QPS. We'll schedule the pilot kick-off for the 2-week window after documents are exchanged.
07:23 Anita: Sounds good. Can you cc our procurement on the NDA?
07:27 Rae: Yes, send names/emails and we'll route the NDA.
07:30 Priya: Anything else on the tech front? I'm interested in seeing the audit log schema.
07:35 Diego: We'll attach the audit schema in the playbook and sample payloads.
07:39 Liam: Cool. One small note — we briefly evaluated DatumCloud and AetherScale; main reason we're talking to Redwood is the routing controls and the private deployment options.
07:50 Maya: Appreciate the context. We'll get the docs out by Monday and propose pilot dates.
07:55 Priya: Thanks everyone. Looking forward.
08:00 Maya: Thanks, bye.

Post-call notes: Mentioned artifacts to share: partner playbook (https://redwood.ai/partners/silkroad-playbook), network integration checklist (doc link placeholder), pilot benchmark harness. Pilot target: 50 QPS steady, spikes to 400 QPS. Security asks: KMS customer-managed keys, audit forwarding, SOC 2 pack.

Recording ends.
